header: Francesca’s customers, girls aged 11 to 15, were growing up faster than the brand. At Phenomenon, we reimagined both the brand and the site around a new idea: Francesca’s as a stylish older sister. I was the visual and product designer.

layout.title: Outgrowing the brand
text: Francesca’s was built for younger girls. But its customers had grown more style-aware and were drifting toward brands like Madewell and Asos. A new look alone wouldn’t fix that. The brand needed a new personality, and the site needed to deliver it at every step of shopping, without alienating parents.

layout.title: A new brand: stylish, not intimidating
text: I designed a brand direction that balanced trend-forward style with approachability: a brighter palette, editorial photography, and a warmer, more confident tone. It tested well across audiences.

layout.title: A new site: shopping like a magazine
text: Working with Phenomenon’s strategists, I carried the brand into the site by taking cues from fashion magazines. I designed an editorial layer that suggested product pairings instead of pushing promotions, so shopping felt like advice from an older sister, not a sales pitch.
In user testing, it was one of the favorite parts of the new site. I also designed a CMS so the Francesca’s team could update the stories and pairings themselves.

layout.title: A smoother checkout
text: I also redesigned the checkout, and we tested several flows with users to find the simplest path to purchase.

layout.title: Result
text: The redesign never launched after the client’s priorities shifted, but the direction held up where it counted. It tested well with both girls and parents, and the editorial layer was one of the most-liked parts of the site in user testing.
